Air Voice Supermarkets Pty Ltd operates a busy a community-oriented IGA supermarket focused on delivering quality products, strong customer service, and a convenient shopping experience. The business places importance on supporting the local community while offering fresh, affordable groceries every day.

An opportunity is available for a driven and capable Store Manager to lead the team and support the ongoing success and growth of our IGA store.

Location: Esperance, WA 6450
Salary: $80,000 to $86,000 per annum plus superannuation
Employment Type: Full-time, permanent

Key Responsibilities

•	Manage daily store operations to ensure smooth and efficient performance 
•	Track sales, margins, and expenses to meet financial targets 
•	Prepare sales projections and oversee budgeting 
•	Lead, support, and motivate staff to maintain high operational and customer service standards 
•	Execute promotional campaigns and merchandising in accordance with IGA guidelines 
•	Oversee pricing, stock management, and inventory control

•	Availability to work weekends, public holidays, and peak periods

Applications open on 27 July 2026 and close on 26 August 2026

About Us 

Amity Care Services is a Mornington Peninsula based disability and home care support provider, founded by a team of registered nurses with extensive clinical experience in complex and acute care. We deliver Supported Independent Living, Specialist Disability Accommodation, Short Term Accommodation, Support Coordination, Psychosocial Recovery Coaching and clinical nursing services across the region, and can provide 24/7 support to our clients. Our values of loyalty, trust and honesty shape how we work with each other and the people we support. 

About the Role 

We are seeking a motivated and organised Rostering Coordinator to join our busy Rostering team at Amity Care Services. 

This role is responsible for coordinating accurate, timely and person-centred rosters for participants and support workers. You will work closely with the Rostering Lead, support workers, participants, families and internal departments to ensure shifts are filled appropriately, participant needs are met, and staffing arrangements remain compliant and sustainable. 

This is a fast-paced role suited to someone who enjoys problem-solving, communicating clearly, working under pressure, and supporting both staff and participants with professionalism and care. 

Key Responsibilities 

Coordinate and maintain participant and staff rosters in line with participant needs, staff availability and service requirements 

Allocate support workers to shifts, including new engagements, ongoing supports, respite and Supported Independent Living arrangements 

Respond to roster changes, cancellations, unfilled shifts and day-to-day staffing issues in a timely and professional manner 

Communicate clearly with support workers, participants, families, coordinators and internal teams regarding roster updates and changes 

Support smooth handovers for new participants, new staff, first shifts and meet and greets 

Monitor staff availability, shift allocations, travel considerations, skills matching and continuity of support 

Maintain accurate rostering records and documentation within VisualCare and related systems 

Escalate concerns regarding participant safety, staff conduct, availability gaps, compliance risks or service continuity to the Rostering Lead or relevant manager 

Work collaboratively with Recruitment, Clinical, Accounts and Management to support safe and consistent service delivery 

Ensure rostering practices align with Amity Care Services policies, NDIS requirements and SCHADS Award considerations 

About You 

We are looking for someone who is calm, organised and confident communicating with a wide range of people. You will be able to manage competing priorities, think quickly, and remain professional when dealing with last-minute changes or complex rostering issues. 

You will bring: 

Ability to work flexibly across a seven-day roster 

Experience in rostering, scheduling, administration or coordination, ideally within disability, aged care, home care or community services 

Strong communication and interpersonal skills 

Excellent attention to detail and time management 

Ability to work in a busy environment and manage competing priorities 

Confidence using computer systems, Microsoft Office and rostering or care management platforms such as VisualCare 

A practical problem-solving approach and the ability to remain calm under pressure 

A genuine interest in supporting vulnerable people in our community 

Understanding of confidentiality, professional boundaries and respectful communication 

Knowledge of the NDIS, SCHADS Award or community services sector would be highly regarded 

Requirements 

NDIS Worker Screening Check and Working with Children Check, or willingness to obtain 

Completed NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission Worker Orientation Module, or willingness to complete 

Current driver licence and reliable transport may be required depending on business needs 

Ability to work from our Mornington Peninsula office 

Why Join Amity? 

Be part of a values-driven, growing organisation making a genuine difference 

Work within a supportive and collaborative team environment 

Contribute to safe, reliable and person-centred supports for participants 

Opportunity to build your skills in rostering, coordination, NDIS service delivery and compliance 

Join an organisation that values loyalty, trust, honesty and continuous improvement 

How to Apply 

To apply, please submit a cover letter and current resume outlining your relevant experience, your interest in the Rostering Coordinator role, and what you believe you could bring to Amity Care Services to recruitment@amitycareservices.com.au.  

Applications close: 3rd August 2026 

For a confidential discussion about the role, please contact Taryn Brien 1800 426 489.

result.description:
## Position Overview
We are looking for a skilled and detail-oriented ICT Systems Test Engineer to join our team and play a critical role in ensuring the quality, reliability, and performance of our technology systems. The successful candidate will be responsible for designing and executing comprehensive test strategies, identifying defects, and working collaboratively with development and infrastructure teams to deliver robust, high-quality solutions. This role suits a methodical and analytical professional with a strong technical background in software and systems testing, a commitment to quality assurance best practices, and the ability to thrive in a fast-paced, agile environment.
## Key Responsibilities
- Specify, develop, and execute detailed test plans, test scripts, and test cases to validate the behaviour, functionality, and integrity of ICT systems across multiple platforms and environments.
- Identify, diagnose, and document functionality errors and faults in systems and programming code within established testing protocols, quality standards, and compliance guidelines to ensure systems perform to specification.
- Design and conduct regression, integration, performance, and user acceptance testing (UAT) to ensure new and updated systems meet defined requirements and business needs.
- Utilise automated test software and frameworks to streamline testing processes, improve test coverage, and increase efficiency across the software development lifecycle.
- Produce clear and comprehensive defect reports, test summary reports, and related quality assurance documentation, ensuring traceability from requirements through to test outcomes.
- Perform systems architecture reviews and assessments, evaluating current and future hardware and software configurations, and contributing recommendations to inform strategic technical direction.
- Collaborate closely with software developers, business analysts, and project managers to clarify requirements, resolve defects, and support timely delivery of system releases.
- Create, review, and maintain technical documentation including procedural guides, operational manuals, instructional materials, technical specifications, and maintenance inventory records.
- Analyse test results and defect trends to identify recurring issues, recommend process improvements, and support continuous quality improvement initiatives across the organisation.
- Participate in agile ceremonies such as sprint planning, stand-ups, and retrospectives, contributing a quality assurance perspective throughout the development cycle.
- Assess risks associated with system changes and releases, providing input into risk mitigation strategies and supporting informed decision-making across project and operational teams.
- Support the evaluation, selection, and implementation of testing tools, methodologies, and frameworks to ensure the organisation's testing capabilities remain current and effective.
## Required Qualifications & Skills
- A bachelor's degree or higher in Information Technology, Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.
- Demonstrated experience in ICT systems testing, quality assurance, or a closely related technical role, with a solid understanding of the software development and systems engineering lifecycle.
- Proficiency in writing and executing test plans, test cases, and test scripts across functional, non-functional, and regression testing scenarios.
- Hands-on experience with test automation tools and frameworks such as Selenium, Cypress, JUnit, TestNG, or comparable technologies.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to diagnose complex system faults and communicate findings clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
- Experience producing high-quality technical documentation, including test reports, defect logs, operational guides, and system specifications.
- Familiarity with agile and DevOps methodologies and the ability to integrate quality assurance activities into iterative development workflows.
- Solid understanding of systems architecture, network infrastructure, and software integration concepts relevant to enterprise ICT environments.
- Competency with defect tracking and test management tools such as JIRA, Azure DevOps, Zephyr, or similar platforms.
- Excellent communication, collaboration, and organisational skills, with a strong commitment to delivering quality outcomes within agreed timeframes.
## Preferred Qualifications
- ISTQB certification (Foundation Level or above) or an equivalent recognised qualification in software testing or quality assurance.
- Experience working in regulated industries or environments with strict compliance, security, or governance requirements, such as government, finance, or healthcare.
- Exposure to performance and load testing tools such as Apache JMeter, LoadRunner, or Gatling.
- Familiarity with cybersecurity testing principles, including vulnerability assessments and secure coding practices.
- Experience with cloud-based environments and platforms such as AWS, Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud, and an understanding of how they impact testing strategies.
- Knowledge of CI/CD pipelines and associated tools such as Jenkins, GitLab CI, or Bamboo.
- A postgraduate qualification or additional certifications in project management, IT governance, or related fields, such as ITIL or PRINCE2, would be highly regarded.
## Why Join Us?
- Be part of a collaborative, inclusive, and forward-thinking team that values technical excellence and continuous improvement, where your contributions directly shape the quality of systems used across the organisation.
- Access ongoing professional development opportunities, including support for industry certifications, training programmes, and attendance at relevant conferences and events.
- Enjoy a flexible working environment with options for hybrid work arrangements, supporting a healthy work-life balance without compromising on career growth.
- Work on complex, large-scale ICT projects that offer genuine variety and the opportunity to deepen your expertise across diverse technologies and industries.
- Receive a competitive remuneration package with a clear pathway for career progression within a growing organisation that invests in its people.
## Job Details
- Job Type: Full-time, Permanent
- Work Schedule: 8-hour shift
- Salary: $70,000 – $120,000 per year + Super

Just Better Care Eastern Suburbs

Full-Time Disabilities Services Officer (Multiple positions)

About us:
Just Better Care provides in-home disability and aged care services, supporting people to live independently. We believe people of all ages & all abilities deserve access to the support and resources they need in order to live where they want and how they want. At Just Better Care, we CARE about our customers and our team. Our office covers four territories in the Sydney Metro area; Eastern Suburbs, Inner West, Sutherland and St George.
Just Better Care Eastern Suburb is looking for Disabilities Services Officer to join our caring and dynamic team. This role involves working with customers to support them in many different aspects of their day-to-day life. The role involves supporting customers with mental, physical, social and emotional disabilities. Support is provided in a manner that maintains the customer’s independence, is respectful and safe.

Main responsibility
• Demonstrate a commitment to best practice, ensuring that all services are provided in a caring and respectful way in accordance with Just Better Care’s policy and procedures.
• Assessing clients' needs and developing individual support plans
• Social support/transportation: social activities, shopping/groceries, travelling to medical appointments
• Clinical support: medication assistance
• Supporting customers in the use of aids and personal equipment including: standing or walking frames, wheelchairs, manual or electric hoists, sliding sheets or moving boards, hearing aids and other physical aids
• Supporting customers with complex and/or challenging behaviours
• Monitoring the well-being of customers and reporting on their progress
• Providing a safe environment for the client by monitoring their surroundings for potential dangers such as fire hazards and tripping hazards.
• Supporting clients socially and arranging visits or outings in the community.
• Ensuring that all documentation is completed in a timely and accurate manner. Where offices are using Mobility Options, community support workers are required to use the application for all schedule visits as per their training.
• Attending and participating in staff meetings and training sessions as directed by the Coordinator.
• Ensuring that all responsible steps are taken to protect personal safety at work and avoid adversely affecting the health or safety of any other person at the workplace in accordance with requirements under the Work Health and Safety legalisation.
• Participating in activities aimed at the continuous improvement of services.
• Complying with Just Better Care’s Vision, Values, and Purpose

What you will need:
• Qualification in the relevant field.
• At least 2 years’ relevant work experience.
• NDIS Workers Check or Police Clearance
• Current Australian Drivers Licence
• Current First Aid and CPR certificates
• Ability to be contacted by either telephone or email
• Ability or willingness to assist or work with customer in daily living and personal care skills
• Be reliable & productive
• Valuing attitudes towards customers
• Ability to work as part of a Team and maintain good working relationships
• Commitment to self-improvement
• Good written and verbal skills in English

Salary Range: $80,000 to 90,000 per annum excluding superannuation.
Why Join Us:
• Close-knit team of friendly, helpful and supportive people.
• Career development and training opportunities are very high on our priority list.
• We have a vested interest in you, hence you will be well supported.
• A competitive salary is on offer for the right candidate.
• Employee Assistance Programme.
If you have any questions or would like to know more about the role, send an e-mail to hr.es@justbettercare.com
